title.zh: 卷304 列傳九十一 张照 甘汝来 陈德华 王安国 刘吴龙 杨汝谷 张泰开 秦蕙田 彭启丰 孙希濂 梦麟
title.en: Volume 304 Biographies 91: Zhang Zhao, Gan Rulai, Chen Dehua, Wang Anguo, Liu Wulong, Yang Rugu, Zhang Taikai, Qin Huitian, Peng Qifeng, Sun Xilian, Meng Lin
title.raw: 卷304 列傳九十一 张照 甘汝来 陈德华 王安国 刘吴龙 杨汝谷 张泰开 秦蕙田 彭启丰 孙希濂 梦麟

sentences.zh: 張照，字得天，江南婁縣人。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhao, style name Detian, was a man of Lou County in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhao, whose style was Detian, came from Lou County in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 康熙四十八年進士，改庶吉士，授檢討，南書房行走。

translations.literal: In the forty-eighth year of Kangxi he passed the jinshi examination, was transferred to Hanlin Bachelor, appointed Compiler, and served in the Southern Study.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi degree in the forty-eighth year of Kangxi, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, was made a compiler, and served in the Southern Study.

sentences.zh: 雍正初，累遷侍講學士。

translations.literal: Early in the Yongzheng reign he was repeatedly promoted to Reader in the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongzheng's reign he rose by stages to Reader in the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 聖祖訓士民二十四條，世宗為之註，題曰聖諭廣訓，照疏請下學官，令學童誦習。

translations.literal: The Sacred Ancestor issued twenty-four injunctions for scholars and commoners; the Shizong annotated them and titled them the Extended Exposition of the Sacred Edict; Zhao memorialized requesting their distribution to educational officials and that schoolchildren recite and study them.
translations.idiomatic: Kangxi had issued twenty-four admonitions for scholars and the people; Yongzheng annotated them under the title Extended Exposition of the Sacred Edict. Zhao submitted a memorial asking that the text be sent down to local schools so pupils could memorize and study it.

sentences.zh: 復三遷刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was again promoted three times to Vice Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted three more times until he reached Vice Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 十一年，授左都御史，遷刑部尚書，疏請更定律例數事。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was appointed Left Censor-in-Chief, transferred to Minister of Punishments, and memorialized requesting several revisions to the penal statutes.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was made Left Censor-in-Chief and then Minister of Punishments, and submitted a memorial proposing several changes to the penal code.

sentences.zh: 大學士鄂爾泰初為雲貴總督，定亂苗，稍收其地，置流官。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Ortai had first served as governor-general of Yunnan-Guizhou, pacified the rebellious Miao, gradually recovered their territory, and established regular officials.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Ortai had earlier been governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou; he had pacified the Miao rebels, gradually brought their lands under control, and installed regular officials.

sentences.zh: 既而苗复叛，揚威將軍哈元生、副將軍董芳討之，不以時定。

translations.literal: Afterwards the Miao rebelled again; the Yangwei General Ha Yuansheng and Deputy General Dong Fang campaigned against them but did not pacify them in time.
translations.idiomatic: The Miao soon rose again. General Ha Yuansheng and Deputy General Dong Fang were sent to suppress them but failed to bring the region under control on schedule.

sentences.zh: 上責鄂爾泰措置不當，照素忤鄂爾泰，因請行。

translations.literal: The emperor blamed Ortai for improper arrangements; Zhao had long been at odds with Ortai and therefore requested to go.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held Ortai responsible for mishandling the situation. Zhao had long been on bad terms with Ortai and seized the moment to ask to go in person.

sentences.zh: 十三年五月，上命照為撫定苗疆大臣。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the thirteenth year the emperor ordered Zhao as Grand Minister for Pacifying the Miao Frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the thirteenth year the emperor appointed Zhao Grand Minister for Pacifying the Miao Frontier.

sentences.zh: 照至貴州，議劃施秉以上為上游，用雲南、貴州兵，專屬元生；

translations.literal: Zhao arrived in Guizhou and proposed to demarcate the region above Shibing as the upper reaches, using Yunnan and Guizhou troops placed solely under Yuansheng's command;
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao reached Guizhou, he proposed dividing the territory above Shibing into an upper zone, assigning Yunnan and Guizhou troops exclusively to Yuansheng.

sentences.zh: 以下為下游，用湖廣、廣東兵，專屬芳：令諸軍互易地就所劃。

translations.literal: below that as the lower reaches, using Huguang and Guangdong troops placed solely under Fang; he ordered all armies to exchange positions and take up their assigned zones.
translations.idiomatic: The area below would be the lower zone, manned by Huguang and Guangdong troops under Fang alone; all forces were to swap posts and deploy according to this division.

sentences.zh: 元生、芳遂議村落道路皆別上下界，文移辨難。

translations.literal: Yuansheng and Fang then debated, marking out separate upper and lower boundaries for every village, road, and hamlet, and wrangling back and forth in official correspondence.
translations.idiomatic: Yuansheng and Fang thereupon quarreled over boundaries, drawing upper and lower limits through villages and roads and exchanging disputatious official memos.

sentences.zh: 照致書元生等，令劾鄂爾泰。

translations.literal: Zhao wrote to Yuansheng and the others, ordering them to impeach Ortai.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao sent letters to Yuansheng and his colleagues instructing them to bring charges against Ortai.

sentences.zh: 會高宗即位，召照還，以湖廣總督張廣泗往代。

translations.literal: Just then the Gaozong Emperor acceded to the throne; Zhao was recalled, and Huguang Governor-General Zhang Guangsi was sent to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Gaozong Emperor took the throne, Zhao was summoned back and replaced by Zhang Guangsi, governor-general of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 上怒照挾私誤軍興，廣泗复劾照謬妄，元生等並發照致書令劾鄂爾泰事，遂奪職逮下獄。

translations.literal: The Emperor was enraged that Zhao had pursued private grudges and disrupted the military campaign; Guangsi again impeached Zhao for absurd conduct; Yuansheng and the others also exposed Zhao's letters ordering them to impeach Ortai; Zhao was therefore stripped of office and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, angered that Zhao had let private motives derail the campaign, accepted Zhang Guangsi's further charge of reckless misconduct; when Yuansheng and others also revealed Zhao's letters commanding them to impeach Ortai, Zhao was dismissed and thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，廷議當斬，上特命免死釋出獄，令在武英殿修書處行走。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Qianlong reign, the court deliberated that he should be executed; the Emperor specially ordered his life spared and had him released, appointing him to serve at the Wuying Hall book-compilation office.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 1 the court recommended execution, but the Emperor personally commuted the sentence, released him from jail, and assigned him to the Wuying Hall editorial bureau.

sentences.zh: 二年，起內閣學士，南書房行走。

translations.literal: In the second year he was reinstated as a Grand Secretariat academician, serving in the Southern Study.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was restored as a Grand Secretariat academician with duties in the Southern Study.

sentences.zh: 五年，复授刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was again appointed vice minister of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was once more made vice minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 照言：「律例新有更定，校刻頒行諸行省，期以一年。

translations.literal: Zhao said: 'The statutes and regulations have been newly revised; proofreading, printing, and distribution to all provinces is expected to take one year.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao memorialized: 'The code has been newly revised; collating, printing, and issuing it to every province will require about a year.

sentences.zh: 舊輕新重者，待新書至日遵行，不必駁改；

translations.literal: Where the old penalty was lighter and the new heavier, wait until the new book arrives before applying it—there is no need to reopen and revise cases;
translations.idiomatic: When an old provision was lighter and the new one heavier, courts should follow the new text only after it arrives, without reopening prior judgments;

sentences.zh: 舊重新輕者，刑部即引新書更正。

translations.literal: where the old was heavier and the new lighter, the Ministry of Justice should immediately cite the new book to correct sentences.'
translations.idiomatic: when the old was heavier and the new lighter, the Ministry of Justice should at once apply the new code to correct sentences.'

sentences.zh: 庶一年內薄海內外早被恩光。

translations.literal: Thus within one year the imperial grace may early reach all within the four seas, near and far.
translations.idiomatic: In this way, within a single year the Emperor's mercy could reach every corner of the realm, at home and abroad.

sentences.zh: 」特旨允行。

translations.literal: A special edict approved and implemented this.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial rescript approved the proposal and ordered it carried out.

sentences.zh: 上以朝會樂章句讀不協節奏，慮壇廟樂章亦復如是，命莊親王允祿及照遵聖祖所定律呂正義，考察原委。

translations.literal: Because the phrasing and cadence of court assembly music did not accord with rhythm, the Emperor feared temple music might likewise be flawed, and ordered Prince Zhuang Yunlu and Zhao, following the Lüli Zhengyi compiled by the Sacred Ancestor, to investigate the origins.
translations.idiomatic: Finding that court ceremonial music was phrased and punctuated out of rhythm, the Emperor feared the same fault in temple music and ordered Prince Zhuang Yunlu and Zhao to trace its foundations according to the Sacred Ancestor's Lüli Zhengyi.

sentences.zh: 尋合疏言：「律呂正義編摩未備，請續纂後編。

translations.literal: Soon they jointly memorialized: 'The compilation of the Lüli Zhengyi is incomplete; we request permission to continue compiling later volumes.
translations.idiomatic: They soon submitted a joint memorial: 'The Lüli Zhengyi remains unfinished; we ask leave to compile a sequel.

sentences.zh: 壇廟朝會樂章，考定宮商字譜，備載於篇，使律呂克諧，尋考易曉。

translations.literal: For temple and court assembly music, determine the gong-shang character notation and fully record it in the text, so that pitch may be harmonized and reference made easy.
translations.idiomatic: For temple and court music, we should fix the gong-shang character notation and set it down in full, so the pitches harmonize and the standards are easy to consult.

sentences.zh: 民間俗樂，亦宜一體釐正。

translations.literal: Popular folk music should also be rectified as one.'
translations.idiomatic: Popular music, too, ought to be corrected on the same principles.'

sentences.zh: 」下部議行。

translations.literal: The memorial was referred to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was sent down to the relevant ministries for review and execution.

sentences.zh: 七年，疏請矜卹軍流罪人妻孥，罪人發各邊鎮給旗丁為奴，其在籍子孫到配所省視，旗丁不得併沒為奴。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he memorialized requesting compassionate relief for the wives and children of criminals sentenced to military exile; criminals sent to border garrisons were assigned to bannermen as slaves, but their registered descendants visiting them at their place of assignment should not also be seized as slaves.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he asked that the wives and children of men banished to military service be shown mercy: though convicts sent to frontier garrisons were given to bannermen as bondsmen, registered descendants who came to visit them at their place of exile were not to be seized and enslaved as well.

sentences.zh: 尋擢刑部尚書，兼領樂部。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to minister of the Ministry of Justice, concurrently heading the Music Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to minister of justice while also taking charge of the Music Office.

sentences.zh: 民間貸錢徵息，子母互相權，謂之「印子錢」。

translations.literal: Among the people, lending money at interest with principal and interest compounding each other is called 'stamp money.'
translations.idiomatic: Private lending at compound interest, in which principal and interest feed upon each other, was known as 'stamp money.'

sentences.zh: 雍正間，八旗佐領等有以印子錢朘所部旗丁者，世宗諭禁革。

translations.literal: During the Yongzheng reign, banner vice-commanders and others used stamp money to bleed their banner soldiers; the Shizong Emperor ordered it forbidden and abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongzheng era some banner vice-commanders had used stamp money to squeeze their troops; the Shizong Emperor ordered the practice banned.

sentences.zh: 都統李禧因請貸錢者得自陳，免其償，並治貸者罪。

translations.literal: Banner general Li Xi therefore requested that borrowers be allowed to confess voluntarily, be exempted from repayment, and that lenders be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Banner general Li Xi then proposed that borrowers be permitted to come forward on their own, be released from repayment, and that the lenders be prosecuted.

sentences.zh: 至是，照言印子錢宜禁，如止重利放債，依違禁取利本律治罪，禧所議宜罷不用，從之。

translations.literal: At this point Zhao said stamp money should be banned; if it was merely usurious lending, punish according to the statute on forbidden interest; Li Xi's proposal should be abandoned and not adopted—the Emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao now argued that stamp money should remain forbidden and that ordinary usury be punished under the statute against illicit interest; Li Xi's scheme, he said, should be set aside—and the Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 九年十二月，父匯卒於家，照方有疾，十年正月，奔喪，上勉令節哀，毋致毀瘠。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the ninth year his father Hui died at home; Zhao was then ill; in the first month of the tenth year he hurried home for the funeral; the Emperor urged him to restrain his grief and not ruin his health.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the ninth year his father Hui died at home while Zhao himself was ill; when he set out in mourning in the first month of the tenth year, the Emperor urged him to govern his grief and not waste away.

sentences.zh: 至徐州，卒，加太子太保、吏部尚書，諡文敏。

translations.literal: Reaching Xuzhou, he died; posthumously awarded Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Minister of Personnel; posthumous name Wenmin.
translations.idiomatic: He died at Xuzhou and was posthumously given the ranks of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and minister of personnel, with the posthumous name Wenmin.

sentences.zh: 照敏於學，富文藻，尤工書。

translations.literal: Zhao was quick in learning, rich in literary talent, and especially skilled in calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao was sharp of mind, fluent in letters, and above all a master of calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 其以苗疆得罪，高宗知照為鄂爾泰所惡，不欲深罪照，滋門戶恩怨。

translations.literal: His offense regarding the Miao frontier—the Gaozong Emperor knew Zhao was hated by Ortai and did not wish to punish Zhao severely, lest it deepen factional animosity.
translations.idiomatic: Though Zhao had fallen afoul of the court over the Miao frontier, the Gaozong Emperor knew Ortai despised him and was unwilling to punish him harshly for fear of inflaming factional rancor.

sentences.zh: 重惜照才，复顯用。

translations.literal: He greatly valued Zhao's talent and again employed him prominently.
translations.idiomatic: Cherishing Zhao's ability, he restored him to high office.

sentences.zh: 及照卒，見照獄中所題白雲亭詩意怨望，又指照集憤嫉語，諭諸大臣以照已死不追罪。

translations.literal: When Zhao died, seeing poems Zhao had composed in prison at Baiyun Pavilion expressing resentment, and also pointing to bitter words in Zhao's collected writings, the Emperor told the ministers that since Zhao was dead, no further punishment would be pursued.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhao's death, the Emperor found poems he had written in prison at Baiyun Pavilion full of grievance and bitter passages in his collected works; he told his ministers that, Zhao being dead, no posthumous penalty would be imposed.

sentences.zh: 後數年，一統志奏進，錄國朝松江府人物不及照，上復命補入，謂：「照雖不醇，而資學明敏，書法精工，為海內所共推，瑕瑜不掩，其文采風流不當泯沒也。

translations.literal: Several years later, when the Comprehensive Gazetteer was submitted, recording figures of Songjiang Prefecture of our dynasty it did not include Zhao; the Emperor again ordered him added, saying: 'Although Zhao was not pure, his natural endowments and learning were bright and quick, his calligraphy exquisite— jointly acclaimed throughout the realm; flaws and merits do not cancel each other—his literary elegance and distinction ought not be erased.
translations.idiomatic: Some years later, when the Comprehensive Gazetteer was presented, its account of Songjiang figures under the dynasty omitted Zhao; the Emperor ordered him restored, saying: 'Zhao was not without fault, yet his gifts and learning were keen, his calligraphy superb, and his reputation widely shared across the realm; merit and blemish do not cancel one another, and such literary grace should not be allowed to vanish.

sentences.zh: 甘汝來，字耕道，江西奉新人。

translations.literal: Gan Rulai, courtesy name Gengdao, a native of Fengxin, Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Rulai, styled Gengdao, was a native of Fengxin in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 康熙五十二年進士，以教習授知縣，補直隸淶水知縣。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the fifty-second year of Kangxi; appointed county magistrate through instructor service; assigned as magistrate of Laishui in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Kangxi 52, entered service as a magistrate through the instructor route, and was posted to Laishui in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 淶水旗丁與民雜居，汝來至，請罷雜派，以火耗補之。

translations.literal: In Laishui banner soldiers and commoners lived intermixed; when Rulai arrived, he requested abolition of miscellaneous levies, compensating with fire-melt fees.
translations.idiomatic: At Laishui banner troops and civilians lived side by side; on taking office Rulai petitioned to abolish assorted surcharges and make up the shortfall from the authorized meltage fee.

sentences.zh: 禁莊田無故增租易佃。

translations.literal: He forbade estate fields from arbitrarily raising rent or changing tenants.
translations.idiomatic: He prohibited manor lands from raising rents or switching tenants without cause.

sentences.zh: 旗丁例不得行笞，汝來請以柳梃約束。

translations.literal: Banner soldiers by regulation could not be beaten with the bamboo; Rulai requested using willow rods for restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Banner soldiers were by rule exempt from the bamboo beating; Rulai asked that they be disciplined instead with willow switches.

sentences.zh: 三等侍衛畢里克調鷹至淶水，居民家，僕捶民幾斃，訴於汝來。

translations.literal: Third-rank bodyguard Bilike came to Laishui with hunting hawks, stayed at a resident's home; his servant beat a commoner nearly to death; the victim appealed to Rulai.
translations.idiomatic: Third-rank guardsman Bilike arrived in Laishui with hunting hawks and lodged in a townsman's house, where his servant beat a civilian nearly to death; the man brought suit before Rulai.

sentences.zh: 畢里克率其僕閧於縣庭，汝來逮畢里克，械其僕於獄。

translations.literal: Bilike led his servant in making a disturbance at the county yamen; Rulai arrested Bilike and shackled his servant in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Bilike marched his servant into the county hall and raised a riot; Rulai seized Bilike and clapped his servant in irons.

sentences.zh: 事聞，下刑部議，奪汝來職，畢里克罰俸，聖祖命奪畢里克職，汝來無罪。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, referred to Ministry of Justice for deliberation—they stripped Rulai of his post and fined Bilike's salary; the Sacred Ancestor ordered Bilike stripped of rank and declared Rulai innocent.
translations.idiomatic: When the case reached the throne, the Ministry of Justice recommended dismissing Rulai and fining Bilike's salary; the Sacred Ancestor stripped Bilike of office instead and cleared Rulai of wrongdoing.

sentences.zh: 汝來自是負循吏名。

translations.literal: From then on Rulai bore the reputation of an upright local official.
translations.idiomatic: From that time Rulai was known as a model local official.

sentences.zh: 移知新安縣，鑿白楊淀堤，溉田數千頃。

translations.literal: Transferred to Xin'an County; excavated the Baiyangdian embankment, irrigating several thousand qing of fields.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Xin'an, he opened the Baiyangdian dike and irrigated several thousand qing of farmland.

sentences.zh: 又移知雄縣，懲奸吏，復請罷雜派。

translations.literal: Again transferred to Xiong County; punished corrupt clerks, again requested abolition of miscellaneous levies.
translations.idiomatic: Later posted to Xiong County, he punished corrupt subordinates and again sought the abolition of miscellaneous exactions.

sentences.zh: 雍正初，授吏部主事，擢廣西太平府知府，三遷至廣西巡撫。

translations.literal: Early Yongzheng, appointed principal in Ministry of Personnel; promoted to prefect of Taiping Prefecture in Guangxi; after three promotions reached Guangxi provincial governor.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Yongzheng he became a principal secretary in the Ministry of Personnel, rose to prefect of Taiping in Guangxi, and after three further promotions became governor of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 五年，遷都察院左副都御史。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, transferred to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was made left vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 汝來為按察使時，李紱為巡撫，奉議州土司羅文剛糾眾阻塘汛，吏請兵捕治，紱與汝來持不許。

translations.literal: When Rulai was provincial judge, Li Fu was governor; Fengyi prefecture native chieftain Luo Wengang gathered crowds to obstruct patrol posts; clerks requested troops to capture and punish; Fu and Rulai held firm against permitting it.
translations.idiomatic: While Rulai served as provincial judge under Governor Li Fu, the Fengyi native chieftain Luo Wengang mustered a mob to block the river patrol posts; the staff asked to send troops to seize him, but Fu and Rulai refused.

sentences.zh: 事聞，世宗命紱、汝來如廣西捕文剛。

translations.literal: When reported, Shizong ordered Fu and Rulai to go to Guangxi to capture Wengang.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, the Shizong Emperor ordered Fu and Rulai to proceed to Guangxi and arrest Wengang.

sentences.zh: 廣西巡撫韓良輔如雲南，與總督鄂爾泰計事，上令汝來署巡撫。

translations.literal: Guangxi Governor Han Liangfu went to Yunnan to consult with Governor-General Ortai; the Emperor ordered Rulai to act as governor.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangxi governor Han Liangfu went to Yunnan to consult Governor-General Ortai, the Emperor put Rulai in charge as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 泗城府土司岑映宸所部民相仇，汝來與鄂爾泰、良輔、紱設謀縶映宸，隸其土流官。

translations.literal: In Sipu Prefecture, subjects under native chieftain Cen Yingchen feuded; Rulai with Ortai, Liangfu, and Fu plotted to arrest Yingchen and subordinate his territory under regular administration.
translations.idiomatic: At Sipu, subjects under the native chieftain Cen Yingchen fell into mutual vendetta; Rulai joined Ortai, Liangfu, and Fu in a plan to seize Yingchen and place his domain under regular officials.

sentences.zh: 汝來請於鎮安土府置學官，上以非苗疆急務，責其沽名。

translations.literal: Rulai requested establishing school officials at Zhen'an native prefecture; the Emperor said this was not urgent for the Miao frontier and rebuked him for seeking reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Rulai asked to appoint school officers in the Zhen'an native prefecture; the Emperor replied that this was no pressing need on the Miao frontier and rebuked him for courting fame.

sentences.zh: 又以汝來謝恩疏言曲賜寬容，上詰之曰：「人君持國法，當行直道，曲則不直，汝來語何意？

translations.literal: Also because in Rulai's thanks-for-grace memorial he said 'graciously granted leniency,' the Emperor questioned him: 'A ruler upholds state law and should walk the straight path—bending means not straight; what do you mean by this language?'
translations.idiomatic: Further, in a memorial thanking the throne for mercy Rulai had written of a 'gracious bending of the law'; the Emperor challenged him: 'A sovereign upholds the law by the straight path; to bend is not to be straight—what do you mean by such words?'

sentences.zh: 」召還京。

translations.literal: He was recalled to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 六年，良輔獲文剛，汝來坐疏縱奪職，在咸安宮官學行走。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Liangfu captured Wengang; Rulai was stripped of rank for laxity, serving at the Xian'an Palace official school.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, after Liangfu captured Wengang, Rulai was dismissed for leniency in the case and assigned to the Xian'an Palace official school.

sentences.zh: 山東巡撫費金吾議濬濟寧、嘉祥、沛縣等處水道，命汝來效力。

translations.literal: Shandong Governor Fei Jinwu proposed dredging waterways at Jining, Jiaxiang, Peixian and elsewhere; Rulai was ordered to contribute effort.
translations.idiomatic: When Shandong governor Fei Jinwu proposed dredging the waterways of Jining, Jiaxiang, Peixian, and other places, Rulai was ordered to assist.

sentences.zh: 九年，起直隸霸昌道。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was reinstated as Ba-Chang circuit intendant of Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was restored as intendant of the Ba-Chang circuit in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，令在任守制。

translations.literal: Upon mourning for his mother, permitted to observe mourning while remaining in office.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he was allowed to observe mourning without leaving his post.

sentences.zh: 再遷禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: Again promoted to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was again promoted to vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，議行三年喪，諮於諸大臣，汝來曰：「三年之喪，無貴賤，一也。

translations.literal: When Gaozong acceded, debating whether to observe three-year mourning, consulting ministers—Rulai said: 'Three-year mourning—without distinction of noble or base—is one for all.
translations.idiomatic: After the Gaozong Emperor's accession, as the court debated observing the three-year mourning rites, Rulai told the assembled ministers: 'The three-year mourning applies without distinction of rank.

sentences.zh: 皇上法堯、舜之道，宜行週、孔之禮，立萬年彝倫之極。

translations.literal: Your Majesty follows the Way of Yao and Shun; you should practice the rites of Zhou and Confucius, establishing the eternal norm of human relations.'
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty takes Yao and Shun as your model; you should enact the rites of the Zhou and of Confucius and fix the everlasting standard of human duty.'

sentences.zh: 」或言二十七月中朝祭大典若有所妨，汝來曰：「墨縗視事，越紼以祭，禮固言之，夫何疑？

translations.literal: Some said that during the twenty-seven months court sacrifices might be hindered—Rulai said: 'Wearing mourning garb while conducting affairs, stepping over the mourning sash to sacrifice—the rites indeed speak of this—what doubt is there?'
translations.idiomatic: When some objected that major court sacrifices during the twenty-seven months of mourning might be impeded, Rulai replied: 'The rites already allow one in deep mourning to govern affairs and, stepping over the mourning cord, to perform sacrifice—what room for doubt?'

sentences.zh: 」乃考載籍，上儀制，援古證今，具有條理。

translations.literal: He then examined records, submitted ritual regulations, citing antiquity to prove the present—all with clear reasoning.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon researched the classics, drafted the ritual protocol, and argued from antiquity to the present with orderly precision.

sentences.zh: 遷兵部尚書，疏言：「廣東海濱微露灘形，民間謂之'水坦'。

translations.literal: Promoted Minister of War; memorialized: 'Along Guangdong's coast where shoals slightly appear, people call them water shoals.'
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to minister of war, he memorialized: 'Along the Guangdong coast, where faint shoals emerge, the people call them water flats.'

sentences.zh: 漸生青草，謂之'草坦'。

translations.literal: When grass gradually grows, called grass shoals.
translations.idiomatic: When grass takes hold, they are called grass flats.

sentences.zh: 徐成耕壤，謂之'沙坦'。

translations.literal: When sand gradually becomes cultivable soil, called sand shoals.
translations.idiomatic: When silt settles into arable ground, they are called sand flats.

sentences.zh: 坦初見，沿海民報圍築者，當先令立標定四至，毋於圍築後爭控。

translations.literal: When shoals first appear, coastal people reporting reclamation should first be ordered to erect markers defining boundaries—no disputes after reclamation.
translations.idiomatic: When a flat first appears, coastal residents who report enclosure and reclamation should first be required to set boundary markers on all four sides, so that disputes do not arise after the work is done.

sentences.zh: 民有田十頃以上，毋許圍築，以杜豪佔。

translations.literal: Commoners with more than ten qing of land may not reclaim—to prevent powerful families' encroachment.
translations.idiomatic: Householders who already hold more than ten qing of land should not be permitted to reclaim, so as to block powerful encroachment.

sentences.zh: 即貧民圍築，限五頃。

translations.literal: Even poor people reclaiming are limited to five qing.
translations.idiomatic: Even the poor, if they reclaim, should be limited to five qing.

sentences.zh: 其出工本牛種助他人圍築量取租息者，聽。

translations.literal: Those providing labor, capital, oxen, seed to help others reclaim and taking proportional rent-interest—permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Those who supply labor, capital, oxen, or seed to help others reclaim land and take rent or interest in proportion may be allowed to do so.

sentences.zh: 陸地開墾例六年昇科，海田浮脃，當寬至十年。

translations.literal: Land reclamation on dry land typically taxed after six years; tidal fields are fragile—should be extended to ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Reclaimed upland is usually taxed after six years, but tidal fields are precarious and the grace period should be extended to ten.

sentences.zh: 潮大至坦沒，蠲一歲糧。

translations.literal: When great tides submerge the shoal, exempt one year's grain tax.
translations.idiomatic: If a high tide submerges the flat, one year's grain levy should be remitted.

sentences.zh: 圍毀則免昇科原額。

translations.literal: If the dyke is destroyed, exempt the original assessed quota.'
translations.idiomatic: If the enclosure is ruined, the original tax quota should be waived.'

sentences.zh: 」疏入，敕廣東督撫議行。

translations.literal: The memorial entered; the Emperor ordered the Guangdong governor and governor-general to deliberate and implement.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, the Emperor directed the Guangdong governor and governor-general to study it and put it into effect.

sentences.zh: 复疏言：「海濱居民單桅船採捕魚蝦，例不輸稅。

translations.literal: He again memorialized: 'Coastal residents in single-masted boats fishing shrimp are by regulation not taxed.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted another memorial: 'Coastal people who fish shrimp in single-masted boats are by rule exempt from tax.

sentences.zh: 近聞各海關監督與雙桅船同令領牌納鈔，又閩、廣間貧民有置𥭋取魚者，有就埠育鴨者，吏或按𥭋按埠私徵稅，請通行嚴禁。

translations.literal: Recently heard each customs superintendent likewise requires double-masted boats to obtain licenses and pay fees; also between Fujian and Guangdong poor people set bamboo weirs for fish or raise ducks at wharves—clerks sometimes levy private taxes by weir or wharf; request universal strict prohibition.'
translations.idiomatic: I have lately learned that customs superintendents are also requiring even double-masted vessels to take licenses and pay dues; and in Fujian and Guangdong poor folk who set fish weirs or raise ducks at the wharves are sometimes taxed privately by the inch of weir or foot of quay—I ask that such levies be strictly forbidden throughout.'

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三年，調吏部尚書，仍兼領兵部，加太子少保。

translations.literal: In Qianlong 3, transferred to Minister of Personnel, still concurrently heading War Ministry, added Junior Guardian of Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 3 he was transferred to minister of personnel while retaining the war portfolio, and was given the rank of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 四年七月，汝來方詣廨治事，疾作，遂卒。

translations.literal: Fourth year seventh month, Rulai had just gone to the yamen to conduct business when illness struck and he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the fourth year, Rulai had just entered his office to transact business when he was seized by illness and died.

sentences.zh: 大學士訥親領吏部，與共治事，親送其喪還第。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Neqin heading Personnel Ministry, conducting business together with him, personally escorted the body home.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Neqin, who shared the personnel portfolio and often worked beside him, personally escorted the body home.

sentences.zh: 至門，訥親先入，嫗縫衣於庭，納親謂曰：「傳語夫人，尚書暴薨於廨矣！

translations.literal: Reaching the door, Neqin entered first; an old woman was sewing clothes in the courtyard; Neqin said: 'Tell the lady—the Minister has suddenly died at the yamen!'
translations.idiomatic: At the gate Neqin went in ahead and found an old woman sewing in the courtyard; he said, 'Tell the lady that the minister has died suddenly at the yamen!'

sentences.zh: 」嫗愕曰：「汝誰也？

translations.literal: The old woman exclaimed: 'Who are you?'
translations.idiomatic: The old woman started and said, 'And who may you be?'

sentences.zh: 」訥親具以告，嫗汪然而泣，始知即汝來妻也。

translations.literal: Neqin told her in full; the old woman burst into tears—it was then learned she was Rulai's wife.
translations.idiomatic: Neqin explained everything; the old woman broke into sobs—it was only then that he realized she was Rulai's wife.

sentences.zh: 訥親因問有餘貲否，嫗曰：「有。

translations.literal: Neqin then asked if there was remaining money; the old woman said 'There is.'
translations.idiomatic: Neqin then asked whether any money remained in the house; she answered, 'A little.'

sentences.zh: 」持囊出所餘俸金，訥親為感泣。

translations.literal: She brought out a bag of remaining salary; Neqin wept with emotion.
translations.idiomatic: She fetched a pouch with what was left of his salary, and Neqin was moved to tears.

sentences.zh: 奏上，上獎其寒素，賜銀千兩，命吏經紀其喪，諡莊恪。

translations.literal: Memorial submitted; Emperor praised their frugal integrity, granted 1000 taels silver, ordered officials manage funeral; posthumous name Zhuangke.
translations.idiomatic: When the account was reported, the Emperor praised their austere integrity, granted a thousand taels of silver, ordered officials to arrange the funeral, and gave him the posthumous name Zhuangke.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶間，汝來曾孫紹烈應順天鄉試，以懷挾得罪，仁宗猶念汝來居官持正，宥紹烈，命仍得原名應試。

translations.literal: During Jiaqing, Rulai's great-grandson Shaolie took Shuntian provincial exam, convicted of carrying crib notes; Renzong still remembering Rulai's upright service, pardoned Shaolie, ordered he still take exam under original name.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jiaqing era Rulai's great-grandson Shaolie, sitting for the Shuntian provincial examination, was convicted of smuggling notes into the hall; the Renzong Emperor, recalling Rulai's upright service, pardoned him and allowed him to keep his name and sit again.

sentences.zh: 陳惪華，字云倬，直隸安州人。

translations.literal: Chen Dehua, courtesy name Yunzhuo, native of Anzhou, Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Dehua, styled Yunzhuo, was a native of Anzhou in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 雍正二年一甲一名進士，授修撰，再遷侍讀學士。

translations.literal: Yongzheng year 2, top-ranked jinshi first in first class; appointed compiler; twice promoted to reader-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 2 he took first place among the first class of jinshi, was appointed a Hanlin compiler, and was twice promoted to reader-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 提督廣東肇高學政，旋調廣韶學政。

translations.literal: Appointed educational commissioner of Zhao-Gao in Guangdong; soon transferred to Guang-Shao educational commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was made educational commissioner for the Zhao-Gao circuit in Guangdong, then soon transferred to the Guang-Shao circuit.

sentences.zh: 遭母喪歸，未終制，召充一統志館副總裁官。

translations.literal: Upon his mother's death he returned home; before the mourning period ended he was summoned to serve as associate director of the Comprehensive Gazetteer bureau.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother died he went home to mourn; before the period of mourning was complete he was called back to serve as deputy chief compiler of the Comprehensive Gazetteer.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，遷詹事，上書房行走，再遷刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong, he was transferred to Grand Mentor and served as an attendant in the Upper Study; he was then transferred again to Vice Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 1 (1736), he was appointed Grand Mentor and attendant in the Upper Study, then promoted again to Vice Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 四年，遷戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he was transferred to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 4 (1739), he was made Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 七年，調兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he was reassigned as Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 7 (1742), he was transferred to Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 八年，以弟德正為陝西按察使，讞獄用酷刑，為巡撫塞楞額所劾。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, because his younger brother Dezheng, serving as Provincial Surveillance Commissioner of Shaanxi, used cruel torture in adjudicating cases, he was impeached by Governor Sai Lenge.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 8 (1743), his younger brother Dezheng, the Shaanxi surveillance commissioner, was impeached by Governor Sai Lenge for employing torture in criminal trials.

sentences.zh: 德正具密摺擬揭部科，為書告惪華，惪華沮之，未奏聞。

translations.literal: Dezheng prepared a secret memorial intending to submit it through the ministry for impeachment, wrote to inform Dehua, and Dehua dissuaded him; it was never reported to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Dezheng drafted a confidential memorial to lodge an impeachment through the ministry and wrote to tell Dehua; Dehua blocked him, and the matter was never reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 上以惪華既知德正事非是，當奏聞，乃為隱匿，非大臣體，且曰：「父為子隱，子為父隱，直在其中。

translations.literal: The emperor said that since Dehua already knew Dezheng's conduct was wrong, he ought to have reported it, yet had concealed it—unbecoming conduct for a great minister—and further said: "A father conceals for his son, a son conceals for his father; therein lies rectitude.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held that Dehua, knowing his brother's conduct was wrong, should have reported it rather than cover it up—conduct unworthy of a senior minister—and declared: "When a father conceals for his son and a son conceals for his father, rectitude lies therein.

sentences.zh: 朕非不知以此風天下。

translations.literal: I am not unaware of using this to instruct the empire.
translations.idiomatic: I do not fail to understand the lesson this would teach the realm.

sentences.zh: 然君臣之倫，實在弟兄之上。

translations.literal: Yet the bond between ruler and minister truly stands above that between brothers.
translations.idiomatic: But the duty between sovereign and minister ranks above even the ties of brotherhood.

sentences.zh: 」下部議奪職，命左遷兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: " The ministry deliberated and recommended stripping his rank; he was ordered demoted to Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: " The ministry recommended dismissal from office; the emperor ordered him demoted to Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 十二年，以議處江西總兵高琦武備廢弛，違例邀譽，奪職。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, he was stripped of rank for deliberating on the punishment of Jiangxi Regional Commander Gao Qi, whose military preparedness had fallen into neglect and who had sought praise in violation of regulations.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 12 (1747), he lost his post over the disciplinary handling of Jiangxi regional commander Gao Qi, whose defenses had been allowed to decay and who had improperly courted commendation.

sentences.zh: 十四年，起為左副都御史，上書房行走。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, he was recalled as Left Assistant Censor-in-Chief and attendant in the Upper Study.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 14 (1749), he was restored to office as Left Assistant Censor-in-Chief and attendant in the Upper Study.

sentences.zh: 以督諸皇子課怠，屢詰責奪俸。

translations.literal: For laxity in supervising the princes' studies, he was repeatedly censured and stripped of salary.
translations.idiomatic: Because he was remiss in overseeing the princes' lessons, he was repeatedly rebuked and docked pay.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，遷工部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, he was transferred to Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 22 (1757), he was transferred to Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，遷禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, he was transferred to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 23 (1758), he was made Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，致仕。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, he retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 29 (1764), he retired.

sentences.zh: 三十六年，皇太后萬壽，詔繪九老圖，以惪華入致仕九老中。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year, on the Empress Dowager's birthday celebration, an edict ordered the painting of the Nine Elders; Dehua was included among the retired nine elders.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 36 (1771), for the Empress Dowager's grand birthday, the court ordered a painting of the Nine Elders, and Dehua was numbered among the nine retired worthies.

sentences.zh: 四十四年，卒，年八十三。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year, he died, aged eighty-three.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 44 (1779), he died at the age of eighty-three.

sentences.zh: 惪華性篤儉，缊袍蔬食，蕭然如寒素。

translations.literal: Dehua was by nature sincerely frugal, wearing patched robes and eating plain vegetables, appearing austere as a poor scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Dehua was genuinely frugal by nature—patched robes, simple fare—and carried himself with the spare dignity of a poor scholar.

sentences.zh: 立身循禮法，而不自居道學。

translations.literal: He conducted himself according to ritual and law, yet did not claim to be a Neo-Confucian moralist.
translations.idiomatic: He lived by ritual and law, but never styled himself a pedant of moral philosophy.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂：「士大夫之患，莫大於近名。

translations.literal: He once said: "The greatest affliction of scholar-officials is cleaving too close to reputation.
translations.idiomatic: He once remarked: "Nothing afflicts the scholar-official more than hunger for a name.

sentences.zh: 求以立德名，則必有迂怪不情之舉而實行荒；

translations.literal: Seeking to establish a reputation for virtue inevitably leads to eccentric and unnatural conduct while real practice falls into neglect;
translations.idiomatic: Seek a name for virtue, and one will resort to queer, unbecoming acts while real conduct goes to waste;

sentences.zh: 求以立言名，則必有異同勝負之論而正理晦；

translations.literal: seeking to establish a reputation through words inevitably leads to disputatious wrangling over differences while right principle grows obscure;
translations.idiomatic: seek a name through doctrine, and one will breed partisan quarrels while the truth is obscured;

sentences.zh: 求以立功名，則必務見所長，紛更舊制。

translations.literal: seeking to establish a reputation through achievement inevitably leads one to flaunt one's strengths and repeatedly overturn old institutions.
translations.idiomatic: seek a name through achievement, and one will parade one's talents and overturn established institutions at every turn.

sentences.zh: 立一法反生一弊，而實行無所裨。

translations.literal: For every law established, a new abuse arises, and in practice nothing is improved.
translations.idiomatic: Each new rule spawns a fresh abuse, and in the end nothing is truly gained.

sentences.zh: 」方為尚書時，京師富民俞民弼死，諸大臣皆往吊。

translations.literal: " When he was Minister, the wealthy commoner Yu Minbi of the capital died, and all the great ministers went to pay condolences.
translations.idiomatic: " While he was a minister, the wealthy Beijing merchant Yu Minbi died, and nearly every senior official went to mourn him.

sentences.zh: 上聞，察未往者，惪華與焉。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of this, he investigated who had not gone, and Dehua was among them.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor learned of it, he checked who had stayed away—and Dehua was on the list.

sentences.zh: 王安國，字春圃，江南高郵人。

translations.literal: Wang Anguo, styled Chunpu, was a native of Gaoyou in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anguo, courtesy name Chunpu, was a native of Gaoyou in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 雍正二年一甲二名進士，授編修，再遷侍講。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongzheng he ranked second among the first class in the jinshi examination, was appointed Compiler, and was again promoted to Lecturer-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 2 (1724), he placed second in the first rank of jinshi graduates, was appointed Compiler, and was soon promoted to Lecturer-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 提督廣東肇高學政，复再遷左僉都御史。

translations.literal: He served as Educational Commissioner overseeing Zhaoqing and Gaozhou in Guangdong, and was again promoted twice to Left Assistant Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He served as educational commissioner for Zhaoqing and Gaozhou in Guangdong, then was twice promoted to Left Assistant Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二年，疏請禁官吏居喪詣省會謁大吏，下部議行。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianlong, he memorialized requesting a ban on officials in mourning visiting provincial capitals to pay calls on senior officials; the ministry deliberated and implemented it.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 2 (1737), he submitted a memorial asking that officials in mourning be forbidden to travel to provincial capitals to pay court to their superiors; the ministry approved and put it into effect.

sentences.zh: 復三遷左都御史。

translations.literal: He was again promoted three ranks to Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted three ranks in succession to Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 五年，兩江總督馬爾泰論廣東巡撫王謩徇縱，命安國往按，即命以左都御史領廣東巡撫。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, when Governor-General Maertai of the Two Jiang charged Guangdong Governor Wang Mo with indulgence and laxity, the emperor ordered Anguo to investigate; he was immediately appointed Left Censor-in-Chief acting as Guangdong Governor.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 5 (1740), when the Two Jiang governor-general Maertai accused Guangdong governor Wang Mo of favoritism and leniency, the emperor sent Anguo to investigate—and at once appointed him Left Censor-in-Chief to serve concurrently as Guangdong governor.

sentences.zh: 安國曰：「吾奉命勘事而即得其位，古所譏蹊田奪牛者非歟？

translations.literal: Anguo said: "I am sent to investigate a matter and immediately receive its office—is this not what the ancients mocked as trampling the field to seize the ox?
translations.idiomatic: Anguo said: "I am dispatched to examine a case and promptly given the post itself—is this not the very thing the ancients ridiculed as 'treading the furrow to take the ox'?"

sentences.zh: 」疏力辭，上不許。

translations.literal: " He memorialized forcefully to decline; the emperor would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized in earnest refusal, but the emperor would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 廣東俗奢靡，安國事事整肅，倉有餘粟。

translations.literal: Guangdong customs were extravagant; Anguo tightened discipline in every matter, and the granaries held surplus grain.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong was a province of lavish habits; Anguo enforced order in all affairs, and the public granaries held grain to spare.

sentences.zh: 故事，自總督以下皆有分，安國獨以非制，止之。

translations.literal: By precedent, from the governor-general downward all received allotments; Anguo alone held this improper and stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: By custom, every official from the governor-general down received a personal share; Anguo alone deemed this irregular and abolished it.

sentences.zh: 九年正月，就遷兵部尚書，尋遭父喪。

translations.literal: In the first month of the ninth year, he was immediately transferred to Minister of War; soon afterward he suffered his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Qianlong 9 (1744), he was promoted on the spot to Minister of War; before long his father died.

sentences.zh: 廣州將軍策楞疏言安國孤介廉潔，歸葬無貲，與護理巡撫託庸等具賻歸之，報聞。

translations.literal: Guangzhou General Celeng memorialized that Anguo was solitary, upright, and incorruptible, and had no funds for burial on returning home; together with Acting Governor Tuoyong and others he provided funeral gifts for his journey home, and reported this to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhou general Celeng reported that Anguo was austere, upright, and poor, and lacked the means to bury his father; he and acting governor Tuoyong and others pooled funeral gifts for his return home and notified the court.

sentences.zh: 十年，召為兵部尚書，調禮部。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, he was recalled as Minister of War and transferred to the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 10 (1745), he was recalled as Minister of War, then transferred to the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 安國疏乞終喪，居廬營葬。

translations.literal: Anguo memorialized begging to complete the mourning period, dwelling in the mourning hut and arranging the burial.
translations.idiomatic: Anguo memorialized asking to finish his mourning, living in the mourning hut and seeing to the interment himself.

sentences.zh: 服闋，乃入朝。

translations.literal: When the mourning period ended, he then entered court.
translations.idiomatic: Only when mourning was complete did he resume attendance at court.

sentences.zh: 十四年六月，安國入對，言諸行省方科試，諸學臣尚有未除積弊。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fourteenth year, Anguo had an audience and spoke of the provincial literary examinations, saying that the educational commissioners still had accumulated abuses not yet removed.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Qianlong 14 (1749), Anguo attended audience and reported that in the provincial examinations, educational commissioners still had lingering abuses that had not been cleared away.

sentences.zh: 上令具疏陳，安國疏言：「上科鄉試後，頗聞諸學臣因錄科例嚴，轉開僥倖。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered him to submit a detailed memorial; Anguo memorialized: "After the previous year's provincial examinations, I have heard that because the rules for the supplementary examination were strict, the commissioners instead opened the door to lucky shortcuts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told him to set it out in a memorial; Anguo wrote: "After last year's provincial exams, I have heard that because the rules governing the follow-up examination were tightened, the commissioners turned instead to back doors and lucky chances.

sentences.zh: 或於省會書院博督撫之歡，或於所屬義學徇州縣之請，或市恩於朝臣故舊，或縱容子弟家人乘機作弊，致取錄不甚公明。

translations.literal: Some curried favor with governors and governors-general at provincial academies; some indulged the requests of prefects and magistrates at subordinate charity schools; some traded favors with ministers' old associates; some allowed sons, younger relatives, and household members to seize the chance to cheat—so that admissions were not very fair or clear.
translations.idiomatic: Some played to governors and governors-general at provincial academies; some bowed to prefects and magistrates at local charity schools; some dispensed favors to old friends of court ministers; some winked at cheating by sons, kinsmen, and household staff—so that selection was far from fair or transparent.

sentences.zh: 」上召安國詢所論諸學臣姓名，安國舉尹會一、陳其凝、孫人龍、鄧釗等。

translations.literal: " The emperor summoned Anguo and asked the names of the commissioners he had cited; Anguo listed Yin Huiyi, Chen Qining, Sun Renlong, Deng Zhao, and others.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor summoned Anguo and asked which commissioners he meant; Anguo named Yin Huiyi, Chen Qining, Sun Renlong, Deng Zhao, and others.

sentences.zh: 上以會一、釗已物故，其凝、人龍皆坐事黜，因責安國瞻徇，手詔詰難。

translations.literal: The emperor noted that Huiyi and Zhao were already deceased, and that Qining and Renlong had both been dismissed for offenses; he therefore rebuked Anguo for favoritism and issued an autograph edict interrogating him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pointed out that Huiyi and Zhao were already dead, and that Qining and Renlong had both been removed for misconduct; he charged Anguo with partiality and sent a handwritten edict pressing him hard on the point.

sentences.zh: 二十年，遷吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, he was transferred to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 20 (1755), he was made Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，疏乞假為父改葬。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, he memorialized requesting leave to rebury his father.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 21 (1756), he asked leave to move his father's grave.

sentences.zh: 上以來年當南巡，諭俟期扈行。

translations.literal: The emperor said that the following year would be the southern tour and ordered him to wait and accompany the procession.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied that he would be making his southern tour the next year and told him to wait and join the retinue.

sentences.zh: 冬，病作，予假治疾。

translations.literal: In winter, illness set in, and he was granted leave to seek treatment.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he fell ill and was granted leave to recover.

sentences.zh: 二十二年春，卒，賜白金五百治喪，諡文肅。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twenty-second year, he died; five hundred taels of silver were granted for funeral expenses, and he was posthumously given the title Wensu.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Qianlong 22 (1757), he died; the court granted five hundred taels of silver for his funeral and conferred the posthumous name Wensu.

sentences.zh: 安國初登第，謁大學士朱軾，軾戒之曰：「學人通籍後，惟留得本來面目為難。

translations.literal: When Anguo first passed the examinations, he called on Grand Secretary Zhu Shi; Shi admonished him: "After a scholar enters the official registers, nothing is harder than preserving one's original face.
translations.idiomatic: When Anguo had just earned his degree, he paid a visit to Grand Secretary Zhu Shi, who warned him: "Once a scholar takes office, nothing is harder than keeping the face you started with.

sentences.zh: 」安國誦其語終身。

translations.literal: " Anguo recited these words all his life.
translations.idiomatic: " Anguo kept those words with him to the end of his days.

sentences.zh: 至顯仕，衣食器用不改於舊。

translations.literal: Even at the height of his career, his clothing, food, and utensils were unchanged from old times.
translations.idiomatic: Even at the summit of power, his dress, diet, and household goods remained what they had always been.

sentences.zh: 深研經籍，子念孫，孫引之，承其緒，成一家之學，語在儒林傳。

translations.literal: He studied the classics deeply; his son Niansun and grandson Yinzhi continued his line of learning and formed a school of their own—the account is given in the Confucian Scholars biography.
translations.idiomatic: He immersed himself in the classics; his son Niansun and grandson Yinzhi carried on his scholarly line and formed a distinctive school of their own, as told in the Confucian Scholars biography.

sentences.zh: 劉吳龍，字紹聞，江西南昌人。

translations.literal: Liu Wulong, styled Shaowen, was a native of Nanchang in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wulong, courtesy name Shaowen, was a native of Nanchang, Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年進士，授庶吉士。

translations.literal: A jinshi graduate in the first year of Yongzheng, he was appointed Bachelor of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Yongzheng 1 (1723) and was appointed a Hanlin bachelor.

sentences.zh: 二年，以朱軾薦，改吏部主事。

translations.literal: In the second year, on Zhu Shi's recommendation, he was transferred to a principal clerk in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 2 (1724), on Zhu Shi's recommendation, he was moved to a principal clerkship in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 六遷至光祿寺少卿。

translations.literal: After six promotions he reached Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: After six promotions he rose to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 嘗視讞牘，有以欲劫行舟定罪者，吳龍曰：「欲劫二字，豈可置人於死？

translations.literal: Once while reviewing case records, there was a man convicted on the grounds of intending to rob a boat; Wulong said: "Can the two words 'intended to rob' be grounds to put a man to death?
translations.idiomatic: Once, reviewing case papers, he found a man sentenced to death on the charge of intending to hijack a boat; Wulong said: "Can the words 'intended to rob' alone justify taking a man's life?"

sentences.zh: 」論釋之。

translations.literal: " He argued for release.
translations.idiomatic: He argued for acquittal.

sentences.zh: 十一年，出為安徽按察使。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, he went out as Provincial Surveillance Commissioner of Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 11 (1733), he was sent out as Anhui surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十三年，內遷光祿寺卿，命管理北路軍需。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, he was transferred within the capital to Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and ordered to manage supplies for the Northern Route army.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 13 (1735), he was recalled to the capital as Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and charged with managing Northern Route military supplies.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，召還，疏言：「北路軍需，有輸送科布多截留察漢廋爾諸處，應就車駝戶追繳腳價。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong, he was recalled and memorialized: "For Northern Route military supplies, there are cases in which transport contractors for Kebuduo, Chahannao'er, and other stations have withheld portions; the cart and camel contractors should be made to repay the transport fees.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 1 (1736), recalled to court, he memorialized: "On Northern Route supplies, contractors hauling grain to Kebuduo, Chahannao'er, and other stations have been skimming deliveries; the cart and camel households should be made to repay the freight charges.

sentences.zh: 尚有逋負，請量予豁除。

translations.literal: There are still outstanding debts; I request that a measured portion be remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Some debts remain beyond recovery; I ask that a portion be forgiven in due measure.

sentences.zh: 」上從其議。

translations.literal: " The emperor followed his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 三遷左都御史，疏言：「步軍統領衙門番役，私用白役，生事害民，宜令具冊考覈，有所追捕，官畀差票，詣有司呈驗。

translations.literal: After three promotions he became Left Censor-in-Chief and memorialized: "Among the runners of the Metropolitan Banner Brigade, private use of unauthorized runners causes trouble and harms the people; they should be required to keep registers for examination and verification, and when pursuing anyone, officials should issue warrants to be presented and verified before the local authorities.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted three ranks to Left Censor-in-Chief, he memorialized: "Runners of the Metropolitan Banner Brigade employ unauthorized men and harass the people; they should be made to keep rolls for audit, and whenever they pursue someone, officials should issue warrants for verification by the local magistracy.

sentences.zh: 步軍統領鞫囚，旗人會本旗都統，民人會順天府尹、巡城御史，互相覺察。

translations.literal: When the Metropolitan Banner Brigade interrogates prisoners, bannermen should be joined by the banner commander of their own banner, and commoners by the Shuntian prefect and the city-patrol censor, so that they may watch and check one another.
translations.idiomatic: When the Brigade examines prisoners, bannermen should be overseen by their own banner commander, and commoners by the Shuntian prefect and the patrolling censor, each keeping watch on the other.

sentences.zh: 」疏入，議行。

translations.literal: " When the memorial arrived, it was deliberated and implemented.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial was sent down for deliberation and adopted.

sentences.zh: 又疏言諸行省州縣董理訟獄，其有舛誤，小民無所申訴，宜令督撫遣監司按行稽考，以申民隱。

translations.literal: He also memorialized that in the provinces, prefectures and counties manage litigation and prisons, and when errors occur the common people have no avenue of appeal; governors and governors-general should be ordered to dispatch surveillance commissioners to tour, inspect, and audit, so as to give voice to the people's hidden grievances.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged that where prefects and magistrates mishandle lawsuits and prisons, ordinary people have nowhere to appeal; governors and governors-general should dispatch surveillance commissioners on inspection tours to audit local justice and bring hidden grievances to light.

sentences.zh: 旋劾罷浙江巡撫盧焯，論如律。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he impeached and dismissed Zhejiang Governor Lu Chao; the sentence followed the law.
translations.idiomatic: He soon impeached and removed Zhejiang governor Lu Chao; the penalty was fixed according to law.

sentences.zh: 遷刑部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 七年，卒，賜白金五百治喪，諡清愨。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he died; five hundred taels of silver were granted for funeral expenses, and he was posthumously given the title Qingbi.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 7 (1742), he died; the court granted five hundred taels of silver for his funeral and conferred the posthumous name Qingbi.

sentences.zh: 吳龍簡重，不苟言笑。

translations.literal: Wulong was terse and grave, not given to idle speech or laughter.
translations.idiomatic: Wulong was spare and solemn, seldom speaking or laughing without cause.

sentences.zh: 為政慎密持重，得大體。

translations.literal: In governing he was cautious, discreet, and steady, grasping the larger principles.
translations.idiomatic: In office he was careful, reserved, and steady, and he grasped the larger principles.

sentences.zh: 督學直隸、江蘇，士循其教。

translations.literal: When he served as educational commissioner in Zhili and Jiangsu, scholars followed his teaching.
translations.idiomatic: As educational commissioner in Zhili and Jiangsu, he shaped the conduct of the scholar class.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初，楊汝穀、張泰開與吳龍先後為左都御史，皆以篤謹被上眷。

translations.literal: In the early Qianlong reign, Yang Rugu, Zhang Taikai, and Wulong successively served as Left Censor-in-Chief, and all were favored by the emperor for their earnest diligence.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Qianlong years, Yang Rugu, Zhang Taikai, and Wulong served in turn as Left Censor-in-Chief, each winning the emperor's trust through sober diligence.

sentences.zh: 楊汝穀，字令貽，江南懷寧人。

translations.literal: Yang Rugu, styled Lingyi, was a native of Huaining in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Rugu, courtesy name Lingyi, was a native of Huaining in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十九年進士，授浙江浦江縣知縣。

translations.literal: A jinshi graduate in the thirty-ninth year of Kangxi, he was appointed magistrate of Pujiang County in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Kangxi 39 (1700) and was appointed magistrate of Pujiang County, Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 行取，授禮部主事。

translations.literal: Selected for capital service, he was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Selected for service in the capital, he became a principal clerk in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 三遷監察御史。

translations.literal: After three promotions he became a supervising censor.
translations.idiomatic: After three promotions he was made a supervising censor.

sentences.zh: 河南南陽鎮標兵以知府沈淵禁博，劫淵，圍諸教場三日。

translations.literal: Soldiers of the Nanyang garrison in Henan, because Prefect Shen Yuan had banned gambling, robbed Yuan and besieged the drill grounds for three days.
translations.idiomatic: At the Nanyang garrison in Henan, troops whose gambling had been banned by Prefect Shen Yuan assaulted him and blockaded the parade ground for three days.

sentences.zh: 汝穀論劾，上遣尚書張廷樞等往按，譴總兵高成誅標兵之首事者。

translations.literal: Rugu memorialized to impeach them; the emperor dispatched Minister Zhang Tingshu and others to investigate, reprimanded Regional Commander Gao Cheng, and executed the ringleaders among the garrison soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Rugu impeached them; the emperor sent Minister Zhang Tingshu and others to investigate, censured regional commander Gao Cheng, and executed the soldier ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 別疏言：「選人待缺，輒言出為人後，或值遠缺，報治喪，冀更選。

translations.literal: In a separate memorial he said: "Candidates awaiting appointment often claim at once that they have been adopted out as heirs, or when assigned to distant posts report that they are in mourning, hoping to be selected again.
translations.idiomatic: In another memorial he wrote: "Candidates waiting for appointment often suddenly claim they have been adopted as heirs, or, when sent to a distant post, report a death in the family, hoping to draw a new assignment.

sentences.zh: 請飭選人具三代，已選，復稱出為人後，報治喪，以不孝論。

translations.literal: I request that candidates be required to submit three generations of lineage; if after selection they again claim adoption as heir or report mourning, they should be judged unfilial.
translations.idiomatic: Require every candidate to submit three generations of lineage; if after appointment he again claims adoption or mourning, let him be punished for unfilial conduct.

sentences.zh: 」下部議行。

translations.literal: " The ministry deliberated and implemented it.
translations.idiomatic: " The ministry approved and put the rule into effect.

sentences.zh: 六遷兵部侍郎，兼署左副都御史。

translations.literal: After six promotions he became Vice Minister of War, concurrently acting as Left Assistant Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: After six promotions he rose to Vice Minister of War, concurrently serving as acting Left Assistant Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 疏言直隸被水災，請運關東米十萬石至天津，留南漕十萬石存河間、保定適中地，分貯備賑。

translations.literal: He memorialized that Zhili had suffered flood disaster and requested that one hundred thousand shi of grain be shipped from the Northeast to Tianjin, and that one hundred thousand shi of southern tribute grain be retained at suitable points in Hejian and Baoding to be stored separately as relief reserves.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that flood had struck Zhili and asked that one hundred thousand shi of grain be shipped from the Northeast to Tianjin, while one hundred thousand shi of southern tribute grain be held at convenient points in Hejian and Baoding and stored in reserve for relief.

sentences.zh: 下部議行。

translations.literal: The ministry deliberated and implemented it.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry approved and carried it out.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，調戶部侍郎，疏言：「河南滎澤地濱黃河，康熙三十六年河勢南侵，縣地多傾陷。

translations.literal: When the Gaozong Emperor ascended the throne, he was transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue and memorialized: "The lands of Xingze in Henan border the Yellow River; in the thirty-sixth year of Kangxi the river shifted south and much of the county's territory collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong took the throne, Rugu was moved to Vice Minister of Revenue and memorialized: "In Henan, the Xingze district lies along the Yellow River; in Kangxi 36 (1697) the river swung south and much of the county sank away.

sentences.zh: 民困虛糧，流亡遠徙。

translations.literal: The people were burdened by taxes on phantom grain and fled far away in exile.
translations.idiomatic: The people were crushed by taxes levied on land that no longer existed, and fled in exile.

sentences.zh: 」上命河南巡撫察議，刪賦額。

translations.literal: " The emperor ordered the Henan governor to investigate and deliberate, and to reduce the tax quota.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor ordered the Henan governor to investigate and recommend cuts to the tax rolls.

sentences.zh: 尋遷左都御史。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was transferred to Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三年，以老乞休，命本省布政使給俸。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qianlong, he requested retirement on account of age; he was ordered to receive salary from the provincial administration commissioner of his native province.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 3 (1738), he asked to retire on grounds of age and was granted salary from his home province's administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 五年，卒，年七十六，諡勤恪。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he died, aged seventy-six, and was posthumously given the title Qinke.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 5 (1740), he died at seventy-six; his posthumous name was Qinke.

sentences.zh: 張泰開，字履安，江南金匱人。

translations.literal: Zhang Taikai, styled Lü'an, was a native of Jinque in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Taikai, courtesy name Lü'an, was a native of Jinque in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 乾隆七年進士，改庶吉士，命上書房行走。

translations.literal: A jinshi graduate in the seventh year of Qianlong, he became a Hanlin bachelor and was appointed an attendant in the Upper Study.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Qianlong 7 (1742), entered the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed an attendant in the Upper Study.

sentences.zh: 旋自編修五遷禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, from Compiler he was promoted five ranks to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: From Compiler he was promoted five ranks in succession to Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 十九年，國子監學錄缺員，泰開舉同部侍郎鄒一桂子志伊。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, when the post of Recorder at the Imperial Academy fell vacant, Taikai recommended Zhi Yi, son of his colleague Vice Minister Zou Yigui of the same ministry.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 19 (1754), when a recorder's post at the Imperial Academy opened, Taikai recommended Zhi Yi, son of his fellow vice minister Zou Yigui.

sentences.zh: 上責其瞻徇，部議奪職，予編修，仍在上書房行走。

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked him for favoritism; the ministry deliberated and recommended stripping his rank, granting him the post of Compiler while retaining him as an attendant in the Upper Study.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked him for partiality; the ministry recommended dismissal from office, and he was reduced to Compiler while remaining an attendant in the Upper Study.

sentences.zh: 二十年，內閣學士胡中藻為詩謗朝政，坐誅，泰開為詩序，授刻，部議奪官治罪，上特宥之，仍在上書房行走。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, Grand Secretary Hu Zhongzao was executed for composing poetry that slandered court affairs. Taikai wrote a preface for the poems and had them carved and printed. The ministry deliberated stripping him of office and punishing him, but the emperor specially pardoned him, and he continued to serve in the Upper Study.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 20 (1755), Grand Secretary Hu Zhongzao was put to death for poetry that slandered the government. Taikai had written a preface for the collection and arranged its printing. The ministry recommended that he be dismissed and punished, but the emperor pardoned him, and he remained an attendant in the Upper Study.

sentences.zh: 尋复授編修。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was again appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon reappointed Compiler.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，擢通政使。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was promoted to Commissioner of the Transmission Office.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 22 (1757) he was promoted to commissioner of the Transmission Office.

sentences.zh: 三遷左都御史。

translations.literal: After three promotions he became Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: After three further promotions he became Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，授禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year he was appointed Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 31 (1766) he was appointed minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，复授左都御史。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year he was again appointed Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 32 (1767) he was again made Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，以老乞休，上獎其勤慎，加太子少傅，賦詩餞其行。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year, citing old age, he requested retirement. The emperor praised his diligence and prudence, added to him the title Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, and composed a poem to send him off.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 33 (1768), pleading age, he asked to retire. The emperor commended his diligence and carefulness, granted him the rank of Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, and wrote a poem to bid him farewell.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，卒，年八十六，諡文恪。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year he died, aged eighty-six, and was posthumously given the title Wenge.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Qianlong 39 (1774), aged eighty-six, and was posthumously titled Wenge.

sentences.zh: 秦蕙田，字樹峰，江南金匱人。

translations.literal: Qin Huitian, courtesy name Shufeng, was a native of Jinque in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Huitian, styled Shufeng, was a native of Jinque in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 祖松齡，順治十二年進士，官左春坊左諭德。

translations.literal: His grandfather Songling was a jinshi in the twelfth year of Shunzhi and served as Left Tutor in the Left Secretariat of the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Songling passed the jinshi examination in Shunzhi 12 (1655) and served as Left Tutor in the Eastern Palace's Left Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 本生父道然，康熙四十八年進士，官禮部給事中，與貝子允禟善，為其府總管。

translations.literal: His biological father Daoran was a jinshi in the forty-eighth year of Kangxi, served as a supervising censor in the Ministry of Rites, was on good terms with Beile Yinshi, and served as chief steward of his household.
translations.idiomatic: His biological father Daoran took his jinshi degree in Kangxi 48 (1709), served as a supervising censor in the Ministry of Rites, was close to Beile Yinshi, and acted as chief steward of his princely household.

sentences.zh: 允禟得罪，逮下獄，蕙田往來省視。

translations.literal: When Yinshi fell from favor and was imprisoned, Huitian went back and forth to visit him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yinshi was condemned and thrown into prison, Huitian visited him repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 世宗貸道然死，而獄未解。

translations.literal: The Yongzheng Emperor commuted Daoran's death sentence, but his case was not yet resolved.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongzheng Emperor spared Daoran execution, but the case against him remained unsettled.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年一甲三名進士，授編修，南書房行走。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong he placed third among the top tier of jinshi graduates, was appointed Compiler, and served in the Southern Study.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 1 (1736) he finished third among the top three jinshi graduates, was appointed a compiler, and served in the Southern Study.

sentences.zh: 乃上疏言：「臣本生父道然身罹重罪，蒙恩曲宥；

translations.literal: He then submitted a memorial stating: "My biological father Daoran committed a grave offense yet was graciously spared by Your Majesty's favor;
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted a memorial: "My biological father Daoran was guilty of a grave crime, yet Your Majesty mercifully spared him;

sentences.zh: 以追銀未完，繫獄九年，年已八十，衰朽不堪。

translations.literal: because the required silver restitution was not complete, he has been held in prison for nine years. He is already eighty, decayed and frail beyond endurance.
translations.idiomatic: because the silver he was ordered to repay was never fully collected, he has remained in prison for nine years. He is already eighty, broken and frail beyond bearing.

sentences.zh: 本年五六月間，浸染暑濕，瘧癘時作，奄奄一息，幾至瘐斃。

translations.literal: During the fifth and sixth months of this year he was afflicted by summer heat and damp; malarial chills and fever recurred, and he lies barely breathing, nearly dead from wasting illness.
translations.idiomatic: Between the fifth and sixth months of this year he was stricken by summer damp and fever; chills and ague came and went, and he now lies at the point of death, scarcely breathing.

sentences.zh: 情關骨肉，痛楚難忍。

translations.literal: This concerns my own flesh and blood; the anguish is unbearable.
translations.idiomatic: This touches my own flesh and blood, and the pain is more than I can endure.

sentences.zh: 臣雖備官禁近，還顧臣父，老病拘幽，既無完解之期，更無生存之望，方寸昏迷，不能自主。

translations.literal: Though I serve in offices close to the throne, when I think of my father—old, ill, and confined in prison—with no prospect of full release and no hope of survival, my mind grows dim and I cannot govern myself.
translations.idiomatic: Though I hold office close to the throne, when I turn my thoughts to my father—old, sick, and shut away in prison—with no prospect of full release and no hope that he will live, my mind reels and I cannot command myself.

sentences.zh: 誠不忍昧心竊祿，內慚名教。

translations.literal: I truly cannot bear to suppress my conscience while secretly accepting salary; inwardly I am shamed before the teachings of moral propriety.
translations.idiomatic: I cannot in good conscience keep my post and draw salary in silence; inwardly I am ashamed before the moral teachings I am bound to uphold.

sentences.zh: 伏惟皇上矜慎庶獄，一線可原，概予寬釋。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that Your Majesty is careful and merciful in all criminal cases; where the slightest thread of justification may be found, release may be granted entirely.
translations.idiomatic: I know that Your Majesty weighs every case with care and mercy, and that where even the thinnest thread of excuse may be found, full clemency may be granted.

sentences.zh: 當此聖明孝治天下，惟有乞恩，匄臣父八十垂死之年，得以終老牖下。

translations.literal: In this age when the sage-like emperor governs the realm through filial devotion, I can only beg for grace—that my father, at eighty and on the verge of death, may end his days under his own roof.
translations.idiomatic: In this age when the sage emperor governs the realm through filial virtue, I can only beg for grace—that my father, at eighty and near death, may be allowed to end his days at home.

sentences.zh: 臣原奪職效奔走以贖父罪。

translations.literal: I am willing to forfeit my office and serve in any capacity to atone for my father's crime.
translations.idiomatic: I am willing to surrender my office and serve in any humble capacity to atone for my father's guilt.

sentences.zh: 」高宗命宥道然，並免所追銀。

translations.literal: The Gaozong Emperor ordered Daoran pardoned and also remitted the silver he was required to repay.
translations.idiomatic: The Qianlong Emperor ordered Daoran pardoned and remitted the silver still owed.

sentences.zh: 蕙田累遷禮部侍郎，丁本生父憂，服將闋，命仍起禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: Huitian was promoted step by step to Vice Minister of Rites; when his biological father died he entered mourning, and as his mourning period was about to end he was ordered to resume office as Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Huitian rose by stages to vice minister of Rites. When his biological father died he entered mourning, and as the mourning period was nearing its end he was ordered back to the same post.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，遷工部尚書，署刑部尚書。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was transferred to Minister of Works and concurrently served as acting Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 22 (1757) he was transferred to minister of Works and concurrently served as acting minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，調刑部尚書，仍兼領工部，加太子太保。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was transferred to Minister of Punishments while still concurrently heading Works, and was given the title Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 23 (1758) he was made minister of Punishments while still heading Works, and was granted the rank of Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 疏請諸行省流匄遞籍編甲收管，上諭曰：「蕙田所奏甚是，為清獄訟、弭盜賊之良法。
